These structures, which embody the essence of traditional Vietnamese court architecture, were meticulously reconstructed in 2000 following the complete destruction of the original ancient campus by war in late 1946.

The Thai Hoc buildings, or Tòa Thái Học, occupy a significant position within the cultural landscape of Hanoi, serving as a living monument to the country’s enduring commitment to education and intellectual pursuits. The architectural splendor of the Thai Hoc buildings is evident in their towering two-story wooden structure, characterized by massive dark-brown wooden columns that support the building’s weight and imbue it with a sense of grandeur.
